questions.question: According to which fundamental right ‘All persons are equal before law’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to Equality.**__

 
• **Right to Equality** is the fundamental right given to the people of India.
 
• **Article 14 **says that the state shall not deny to any person equality before the law and equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.
 
• This provision **confers rights on all persons whether citizens or foreigners.**
 
• Other articles under Rigt to equality - 
 
 
• **Article 15** - Prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.
 
• **Article 16** - Equality of opportunity in matters of public employment.
 
• **Article 17** - Abolition of untouchability and prohibition of its practice.
 
• **Article 18** - Abolition of titles except military and academic.
 
 
 
• The concept of** 'equality before law'** is an element of the concept of the concept of 'Rule of Law' propounded by A**.V. Dicey**, the British jurist.
 
• **Article 19 to 22** describes Right to freedom.
 
• **Article 29 and 30 **describes Cultural and educational rights.
 
• **Article 23 and 24 **describes Right against exploitation.

questions.question: Directive principles of state policy are enumerated in which part of Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Part IV.**__

 
• **Directive Principle of State Policy** is enumerated in **Part IV** of the Constitution.
 
• It is mentioned under** Articles 36 to 51.**
 
• The idea is borrowed from the **Irish Constitution of 1937,** which had copied it from the Spanish Constitution.
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy is the **guidelines or principles **that the state should keep in mind while formulating policies and enacting laws.
 
• These are the constitutional instruction or recommendations to the legislature, executive and administrative manner.
 
• It resembles the **'Instrument of Instructions' present in the Government of India Act of 1935.**
 
• The Directive Principles are** non-justiciable** in nature, that is not legally enforceable by courts for their violation.
 
• On the basis of the content, Directive Principle can be classified into three broad categories such as **socialistic, Gandhian and liberal - intellectual.**
 
• The Directive Principles along with Fundamental rights contains the philosophy of Constitution and is the **soul of the Constitution.**
 
• **Dr B.R. Ambedkar **describes it **as 'novel feature.**

questions.question: In last years of his reign Akbar was distracted by the rebellion of Prince Salim, The future emperor _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Jahangir**

**Explanation:**

Prince Salim, the future emperor Jahangir; distracted Akbar during the last years of his reign. In the later years of his reign, Akbar the Great, the third ruler of the Mughal Empire, faced a significant challenge in the form of a rebellion led by his own son, Prince Salim. This period of rebellion and conflict occurred in the early 17th century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Prince Salim, who later ascended to the Mughal throne as Emperor Jahangir, had a strained relationship with his father Akbar. The conflict arose due to various factors, including Salim's ambition for power, dissatisfaction with his position in the empire, and disagreements with Akbar over matters of governance and succession.
 
• The rebellion by Prince Salim, also known as the Prince Salim Revolt or the Khusrau Rebellion, took place in 1600-1601. Salim sought support from various factions, including disenchanted nobles, to challenge Akbar's authority. However, the rebellion was eventually suppressed by Akbar's forces, and Salim was reconciled with his father.
 
• Despite the reconciliation, the strained relationship between Akbar and Salim persisted, and Akbar's health declined in the subsequent years. Akbar passed away in 1605, and upon his death, Prince Salim ascended to the Mughal throne as Emperor Jahangir.

Jahangir's reign, which lasted from 1605 to 1627, is known for its cultural richness, marked by art, literature, and architecture. Despite the earlier conflicts with his father, Jahangir's rule is considered a period of relative stability and cultural flourishing within the Mughal Empire. The intricate dynamics of the father-son relationship between Akbar and Jahangir and the events leading to the ascension of Jahangir are essential aspects of Mughal history during this period.

questions.question: The tricuspid valve occurs between the ______.
questions.solution:
The tricuspid valve, or right atrioventricular valve, is on the right dorsal side of the mammalian heart, between the right atrium and the right ventricle.

__**Explanation-**__

__
 
• The tricuspid valve is one of the four valves in the human heart, which ensure that blood flows in the correct direction.
 
• Specifically, the tricuspid valve is located between the **right atrium and the right ventricle.**
 
• Its name "tricuspid" comes from its three flaps or leaflets (known as cusps) that open and close.
 
• The main function of the tricuspid valve is to prevent the backflow of blood. When the heart is in** diastole **(relaxed and the chambers are filled with blood), the tricuspid valve opens, allowing blood to move from the right atrium to the right ventricle. When the heart moves into **systole** (and the ventricles are contracting to pump blood), the tricuspid valve closes to prevent blood from moving back into the atrium.
 
• **Disorders** of the tricuspid valve may include tricuspid stenosis (narrowing, preventing enough blood from moving into the right ventricle) or tricuspid regurgitation (leaking, which allows blood to flow back into the right atrium when the right ventricle is contracting).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Tricuspid Valve:** This is located between the right atrium and it opens to allow deoxygenated blood to flow from the right atrium into the right ventricle when the heart is relaxed during diastole. 
 
• **Pulmonary Valve (Pulmonic Valve): **It is located at the opening of the right ventricle into the pulmonary artery. It opens to allow deoxygenated blood to flow from the** right ventricle into the pulmonary artery** and onwards to the lungs when the ventricle contracts. Upon relaxation of the right ventricle, the valve closes to prevent backflow from the pulmonary artery.
 
• **Mitral Valve (also known as Bicuspid Valve): **It is located between the** left atrium and the left ventricle.** This valve has two cusps and works similarly to the tricuspid valve. During diastole, it opens to let oxygenated blood from the left atrium into the left ventricle. Then, during systole (ventricular contraction), the mitral valve closes to prevent blood from flowing back into the left atrium.
 
• **Aortic Valve: **It is located at the opening of the left ventricle into the aorta (the largest artery in the body). It allows oxygenated blood to flow from the **left ventricle into the aorta** and then to the rest of the body when the ventricle contracts. When the ventricle relaxes, the aortic valve closes to prevent the backflow of blood from the aorta.

questions.question: The focal length of a plane mirror is ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **infinity**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Plane Mirror:

 
• A plane mirror is a mirror with a flat (planar) reflective surface.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6e21dcba1897bafbecbfea00b8702e9311fa987d3264baa2f85a1e3c1de579be.png] 

The characteristics of an image formed in a plane mirror:

 
• The image formed by the plane mirror is virtual and erect i.e. image cannot be projected or focused on a screen.
 
• The focal length of the plane mirror is infinite.
 
• The distance of the image ‘behind’ the mirror is the same as the distance of the object in front of the mirror.
 
• The size of the image formed is the same as the size of the object.
 
• The image is laterally inverted, i.e. left hand appears to be the right hand when seen from the plane mirror.
 
• If the object moves towards (or away from) the mirror at a certain rate, the image also moves towards (or away from) the mirror at the same rate.

questions.question: Gold is alloyed with which metal to make it harder?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:-**__

 
• Alloys are a fundamental concept in metallurgy and materials science. An alloy is a mixture of two or more elements where at least one of them is a metal. Alloys are designed to have properties that are better fitted for specific uses than the pure elements themselves.
 
• Gold is a highly malleable and ductile metal, properties that while often beneficial, can lead to deformations in items such as jewelry or coins which are under constant physical stress. Pure gold (24 carat gold) is too soft for producing functional items and can easily get scratched. So, to enhance its hardness and durability, it's combined with other harder metals to make an alloy.
 
• The proportion of gold in the alloy is usually quantified in carats (K), where 24K represents pure gold. An 18K gold alloy typically includes 75% gold, with the remaining 25% being made up of copper, silver, and/or other metals.

 

**Explanation:-**

The pure gold is too soft on its own and is therefore hardened by the addition of alloying elements, copper, silver, nickel, palladium and zinc.

On the other hand:

 
• Sn (Tin) is not usually used in gold alloys used in jewelry due to its relatively low melting point and softness.
 
• Na (Sodium) is a highly reactive metal and is not used in gold alloys.
 
• C (Carbon) is a non-metal and doesn't alloy with gold in the traditional sense.
